 WATCH: Jasprit Bumrah castles Tom Latham in first over of first Test
 Jasprit Bumrah struck on the third ball of the first over at Basin Reserve on November 19, sending New Zealand captain Tom Latham's off stump out of the ground for a duck.
 By CricTracker Staff Published - 19 Nov 2026, 03:59 IST 
 2 Min Read
 Jasprit Bumrah and Tom Latham. (Photo Source: Sony Liv) 0 0 Jasprit Bumrah removed New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck off the third delivery of the very first over in the opening Test between India and New Zealand at Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19. The ball was a good-length delivery that angled back sharply into the right-hander. Latham chose to leave it, only for the seam to hold its upright position and clip the off stump out of the ground.
 The dismissal handed India an immediate advantage after Shubman Gill , captaining the side, had won the toss and elected to bowl first. The wicket also marked Bumrah's first Test appearance of 2026, making the breakthrough all the more significant as he returned to the longest format this year.
 Some introductions are best made with a BOOM. 💥 
Tom Latham gets a taste of Jasprit Bumrah's brilliance in the very first over!

 How did Bumrah dismiss Latham so early?
 The delivery that ended Latham's innings was a precise piece of seam bowling. Bumrah pitched it on a good length and angled the ball back into the right-hander, maintaining a perfect seam position on the Basin Reserve surface. Latham appeared to read the original line and opted not to play a stroke, but the ball straightened just enough off the pitch to beat the inside edge and disturb the off stump, leaving the New Zealand captain stranded on nought.
 The wicket arrived on the third ball of the opening over, placing New Zealand under immediate pressure at the top of their innings. Bumrah's ability to generate movement from the Basin Reserve surface within the first few minutes of play reinforced Gill's decision to put the opposition in after winning the toss. It was a reminder of why Bumrah remains one of the most difficult new-ball bowlers to face in Test cricket, particularly when conditions offer even modest assistance off the pitch.
 What is India's Test record at Basin Reserve?
 India's history at Basin Reserve adds considerable context to this match. The last time India claimed a Test victory at this ground was in February 1968, making it one of the longest gaps between wins at a single overseas venue in their Test history. Beyond Wellington, India have not won a Test match in New Zealand in March since 2009, underlining the consistent difficulty touring sides from the subcontinent have faced in these conditions over the decades.
 The early wicket from Bumrah offered India a positive start in their pursuit of ending that extended wait for a Basin Reserve victory. Whether the hosts can recover from the loss of their captain without scoring will be a key theme as the first day's play unfolds.
